subtitle: One repo, one agent product: Spring Boot AI services streaming to React, tool endpoints, and auth — ship a full-stack agent from database to UI
audience: Developers who finished Spring AI for E-commerce (ChatClient, advisors, tools, RAG) and now own the whole vertical: Java backend, streaming React frontend, per-user threads, and tenant-safe auth. Java/React run in your project (Spring AI 1.1+/2.x verified basis, React 19); protocol machinery (SSE parsing, auth headers, budgets) runs as executable JS in the playground.
outcomes: Lay out one repo (api/web/shared contracts) with versioned boundaries between halves
Design Boot endpoints: sync JSON, SSE streaming, tool endpoints with validation and audit
Authenticate per-user threads (JWT sessions, tenant isolation, conversation ownership)
Stream to React: EventSource parsing, optimistic UI, citations rendering, reconnect discipline
Persist conversations (threads, messages, checkpoints) in Postgres with ownership checks
Evaluate full-stack with gold conversations spanning UI states and API contracts
Guard the vertical: PII redaction end to end, rate limits per tier, CORS/CSRF posture
Ship with deploy gates: contract tests (OpenAPI), canary, rollback, and the launch bundle

assessment.q: One repo, two halves. Boundary rule?
options: Versioned contracts (OpenAPI + event shapes) between api/ and web/; halves evolve independently behind the contract
assessment.explain: Contracts version UI/API evolution independently: breaking changes migrate with deprecation, not coordination meetings (Ch.1).

assessment.q: Streaming endpoint needs entity records. Pattern (per Spring course)?
options: Stream strings (SSE) → collect client-side → validate/convert explicitly; typed UI state from parsed entities
assessment.explain: Collect-then-convert bridge, now split across the wire: SSE text frames, client assembly, schema validation before render (Ch.2/4).

assessment.q: User B reads user A's thread by guessing IDs. Missing?
options: Ownership checks: every thread/message query scoped by authenticated user/tenant — authorization per row, never by obscurity
assessment.explain: Tenant isolation is per-query WHERE clauses on owner, enforced server-side. Obscure IDs are not access control (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Stream drops mid-reply on flaky mobile. UX?
options: Reconnect with Last-Event-ID resume + partial-render preservation: dropped streams resume, never restart from zero
assessment.explain: SSE resume (Last-Event-ID) plus client-side partial state turns drops into pauses. Restart-from-zero wastes money and patience (Ch.4).

assessment.q: Tool endpoint mutates on GET. Violations?
options: HTTP semantics + safety: mutations via POST with validation, idempotency keys, audit; GET stays side-effect free (and cacheable)
assessment.explain: Method semantics protect against prefetch/crawl-triggered mutations. Side effects ride POST with keys and audit (Ch.5).

assessment.q: Conversations table without owner column ships. Consequence?
options: Unfixable-later cross-tenant reads: ownership must exist from row one — retrofitting isolation rewrites history
assessment.explain: Isolation is a day-one schema decision: owner columns + RLS/predicates from the first migration. Retrofits leak during the gap (Ch.6).

assessment.q: Gold covers API JSON but UI shows stale drafts. Missing layer?
options: UI-state gold: streamed frames → rendered states incl. reconnect/resume paths — full-stack eval spans the wire
assessment.explain: Full-stack truth lives in rendered states: frames assembled, citations shown, resume paths preserved. API-only gold misses the UI half (Ch.7).

assessment.q: PII in browser localStorage for 'offline mode'. Verdict?
options: XSS-readable PII at rest without HttpOnly protection: tokens in memory/HttpOnly, PII server-side, storage audited per key
assessment.explain: Browser storage threat model: XSS reads localStorage. Secrets never persist client-side; PII minimized with per-key justification (Ch.7).

assessment.q: Contract test fails on new optional field. Response?
options: Additive changes pass with tolerance (unknown-field ignoring); breaking changes version + deprecate — contracts evolve, never surprise
assessment.explain: Additive (optional fields) vs breaking (renames/removals): tolerance for the former, versioning for the latter. Contract tests enforce the distinction (Ch.8).

assessment.q: Launch bundle missing rollback procedure. Verdict?
options: Blocked: unrehearsed rollback is hope; previous gold-passing version redeployable in minutes, proven by drill
assessment.explain: Reversibility gates launches: drilled rollback paths with version pins. Hope is not a deployment strategy (Ch.8).

project.title: The Storefront Agent Product
project.summary: Ship one repo containing a Spring Boot AI service layer and a React assistant UI: JWT-secured threads, SSE streaming with resume, tool endpoints with audit, Postgres-persisted conversations, gold-evaluated UI states, and a launch bundle. Database to UI, measured end to end.
requirements: Repo layout api/web/shared with versioned OpenAPI + event-shape contracts
Auth: JWT sessions, per-user thread ownership enforced per query, tenant-scoped data
Streaming chat UI: SSE parsing, optimistic states, citation rendering, Last-Event-ID resume
Tool endpoints: validated POST mutations with idempotency keys + audit; read endpoints cacheable
Persistence: threads/messages/checkpoints in Postgres with owner columns from migration one
Evaluation: API contract tests + UI-state gold (frames → rendered, incl. reconnect) + no-regression gates
Guardrails: PII redaction end to end, rate limits per tier, CORS/CSRF posture documented
technical: Version basis pinned (Spring AI 1.1+/2.x, Boot 3.x, Java 17+, React 19); deviations documented
Protocol machinery (SSE parsing, auth headers, budgets) demonstrated runnable in JS
Secrets server-side only; browser storage audited per key; PII scrubbed in logs and fixtures
Numbers reproducible: gold sets, budgets, eval scores committed
project.architecture: Five sections: (1) Repo map — halves, contracts, versions; (2) Runs — traced conversations across UI states with per-layer attribution; (3) Evaluation — API + UI gold with diffs and gates; (4) Operations — auth, persistence, budgets, runbooks; (5) Launch evidence — scores, gates, residual risks with owners.
steps: Lay out repo + contracts first (OpenAPI, event shapes); scaffold health endpoints both halves
Build auth + thread ownership with negative tests (cross-user reads refused)
Add streaming chat UI with resume; prove reconnect preserves partials
Add tool endpoints with validation/audit; persist conversations with owner columns
Write API + UI gold; baseline; iterate once on weakest segment; re-score
Assemble launch bundle (gates, runbooks, residual risks) and red-team it
evaluation: Cross-user thread reads refused (proven, not assumed); tenant isolation per query
Reconnect preserves partials with Last-Event-ID; citations render from parsed entities
Tool mutations validated + idempotent + audited; reads cacheable per method semantics
Gold covers API contracts AND UI states incl. reconnect; no-regression gates hold
PII absent from logs/fixtures/storage; rate limits tiered with honest statuses
stretch: Add a second model route (cost/quality) with per-tier selection and measured savings
Offline-first queue: outbox pattern for flaky networks with conflict rules
Voice input path with the same contracts (modality added, architecture unchanged)

interviewQs.q: SSE vs WebSocket for agent streaming — decide.
interviewQs.a: SSE for server→client token streams (simple, HTTP-native, auto-reconnect with Last-Event-ID, firewall-friendly); WebSockets when clients must also stream up continuously (voice, collaborative editing). Agent chat is overwhelmingly server-push: SSE by default, WebSockets only for bidirectional needs. Decide by directionality, not fashion.

interviewQs.q: How do you keep one user's threads from another?
interviewQs.a: Owner columns from migration one, every query scoped by authenticated user/tenant server-side, negative tests proving cross-user reads refuse, JWT sessions with short expiry + refresh rotation, and audit on thread access. Obscurity (unguessable IDs) is not a layer — enforcement is per-query predicates plus tests.

interviewQs.q: Streaming UX on flaky networks — design it.
interviewQs.a: EventSource with Last-Event-ID resume, client-side partial state preserved across drops, optimistic send states with server reconciliation, reconnect backoff with visible status, and idempotent sends (client-generated IDs deduped server-side). Drops become pauses: resume, never restart — verified by chaos tests killing mid-stream.

interviewQs.q: Where do entities get validated in a streaming flow?
interviewQs.a: Twice: incrementally lenient during streaming (partial renders marked provisional), strictly on completion before state commit and render-finalize. Collect-then-convert bridge with schema validation at assembly; invalid finals route to repair-or-quarantine, never into UI state. Validation placement follows data finality.

interviewQs.q: Contract tests between web/ and api/ — what breaks them legitimately?
interviewQs.a: Additive changes (optional fields) pass with tolerance; breaking changes (renames, removals, type changes) fail and force versioning + deprecation. Legitimate breaks carry migration notes and dual-serve windows. Tests enforce the distinction so evolution stays deliberate, and frontend/backend deploy independently behind versions.

interviewQs.q: PII in a full-stack agent product — map every touchpoint.
interviewQs.a: Browser storage (minimize, justify per key, never secrets), network (TLS, redacted logs), server logs (scrubbed mappers), eval fixtures (scrubbed identically), database (encrypted at rest, owner-scoped access), caches (tenant-isolated keys), error reports (scrubbed). Each touchpoint has a rule; audit walks the list quarterly.
